_about: Submersibles data for the Eveniunt Command Center, built by tools/submarines.py from pinned sources (data/SOURCES.md). Ids are the game's row ids: sectors and seas from SubmarineExploration and SubmarineMap, parts from SubmarinePart, items from Item. Sector names are the game's, with the italic markers around three ship names removed. Sector fields: rank = rank required, tanks = ceruleum tanks, survey = survey minutes, exp = experience reward (base value), surveyDistance = range the survey uses, x/y/z = position. Each table names its source and commit in 'tables'.

unlocks.note: by = the sector whose survey can reveal this one; start = open from the beginning; extraSub = surveying this sector grants permission for one more submarine; opensSea = surveying this sector opens that sea; mainPath = on the source's main line through the seas. The source says discovery is not certain on every visit. The owner's own ticks on the return sheet are what the app treats as true for each Free Company (design 5.4).

subSlots.label: community data
subSlots.note: Submarine slot 2, 3 and 4 and the sector whose survey grants each, in the order they come. The source adds that a new slot only shows once the previous one holds a submarine.

formula.label: calculated, not yet confirmed
steps: A route starts at its sea's starting point and visits 1 to 5 sectors of that sea in the order chosen.
Leg length: the straight-line distance between two points, from their X, Y and Z positions.

Range used: for each leg, round down (leg length x 0.035), then add the destination's survey distance; add up every leg. The route is reachable if the total is no more than the build's range. There is no leg back.
Speed: the build's speed (four parts plus the rank's bonus); a speed below 1 counts as 1.
Travel seconds of a leg: round down (leg length x 3990 / (speed x 100) x 60).
Survey seconds of a sector: round down (survey minutes x 7000 / (speed x 100) x 60).
Voyage seconds: every leg's travel seconds plus every sector's survey seconds, plus a fixed 43,200 seconds (12 hours).
Return time: the send time plus the voyage seconds.
formula.experienceNote: The game table gives each sector's base experience. Submarine Tracker (Data/Sectors.cs) adds 25%, 50%, 75% or 100% to a sector's experience when its survey goes well, judged against surveillance, retrieval and favor thresholds that it takes from a community spreadsheet with no stated licence; those thresholds are not used here. By that source, base experience is the least a voyage gives, so a rank worked out from it is a floor; the return sheet's rank check shows the real figure (design assumption A4).
formula.precision: The source computes in single precision (C# float); this file's checks use double precision. The two can differ by one second only when a value falls a hair away from a whole second; the five test voyages give the same seconds either way.
